questions.question: State the contributions of Robert Koch and outline Koch’s postulates.
questions.solution_html:
• State the contributions of Robert Koch and outline Koch’s postulates.
  • Answer
  • Contributions of Robert Koch
  • Robert Koch is known as the Father of Medical Microbiology. His major contributions include:
  • • Established the germ theory of disease.
  • • Identified Bacillus anthracis as the cause of anthrax.
  • • Discovered Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative agent of tuberculosis.
  • • Identified Vibrio cholerae as the causative organism of cholera.
  • • Developed pure culture techniques.
  • • Introduced staining methods and solid culture media.
  • Koch’s Postulates

questions.question: Define putrefaction and explain its significance in meat spoilage.
questions.solution_html:
• Define putrefaction and explain its significance in meat spoilage.
  • Putrefaction is the microbial decomposition of proteins present in meat, resulting in the
  • formation of foul-smelling compounds.
  • Significance in Meat Spoilage
  • • Produces ammonia, hydrogen sulfide, indole and skatole.
  • • Causes offensive odours.
  • • Alters flavour and texture.
  • • Reduces nutritional quality.
  • • Makes meat unsuitable for consumption.

questions.question: Describe the role of moisture in spoilage of stored cereal grains. [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role of moisture in spoilage of stored cereal grains.
  • Moisture plays a major role in grain spoilage.
  • Effects of High Moisture
  • • Promotes growth of moulds and bacteria.
  • • Increases respiration of grains.
  • • Causes heating and caking.
  • • Encourages insect infestation.
  • • Leads to production of mycotoxins such as aflatoxins.
  • • Reduces shelf life and quality.
  • Prevention
  • • Maintain grain moisture below 13–14%.
  • • Store in dry and well-ventilated conditions.
  • [5x4 = 20]

  • Characteristics

  • • Motile with polar flagellum.
  • • Non-spore-forming.
  • • Facultative anaerobe.
  • Sources
  • • Contaminated water.
  • • Contaminated food.
  • • Poor sanitation systems.
  • Transmission
  • Occurs through the fecal-oral route by consuming contaminated food and water.
  • Pathogenesis

questions.question: Describe the spoilage of milk with reference to acid, proteolytic, and gas-forming spoilage. [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the spoilage of milk with reference to acid, proteolytic, and gas-forming spoilage. Answer Introduction Milk is a highly nutritious food and serves as an excellent medium for microbial growth, leading to spoilage. A. Acid Spoilage Causative Organisms
  • • Lactobacillus
  • • Lactococcus
  • • Streptococcus Process Lactose is converted into lactic acid. Effects
  • • Sour taste.
  • • Increased acidity.
  • • Coagulation of casein.
  • • Curd formation. B. Proteolytic Spoilage Causative Organisms
  • • Pseudomonas
  • • Bacillus
  • • Clostridium Process Proteins are broken down by microbial enzymes. Effects
  • • Bitter taste.
  • • Putrid odour.
  • • Texture deterioration. C. Gas-forming Spoilage Causative Organisms
  • • Coliform bacteria
  • • Clostridium species
  • • Certain yeasts Process Fermentation of lactose produces carbon dioxide and hydrogen. Effects
  • • Swollen containers.
  • • Foaming.
  • • Unpleasant taste and odour. Prevention of Milk Spoilage
  • • Proper pasteurization.
  • • Refrigerated storage.
  • • Hygienic handling and packaging. [10x2 = 20]
